s1.syndrome_frame: Acute left flank pain with cyclical fevers and cardiac mass
salient_findings: Left ventricular mass on cardiac imaging
key_facts: 22-year-old man with no significant medical history
1 day of acute left flank pain
Developed cyclical fevers while hospitalized
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase
Malignant spindle cell tumor on immunostains
SS18 (SYT;18q11.2) translocation on cytogenetics
Immunohistochemistry positive for epithelial membrane antigen (EMA)
Renal infarction on computed tomography
Large left ventricular mass on trans-thoracic echocardiography
Pedunculated LV mass on trans-esophageal echocardiography
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed mass location

shortlist.label: Synovial sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant spindle cell tumor with SS18 (SYT;18q11.2) translocation

shortlist.label: Cardiac myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large left ventricular mass on imaging studies

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant spindle cell tumor with epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) positivity

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant spindle cell tumor with potential for cardiac metastasis

raw.rationale: The presence of SS18 (SYT;18q11.2) translocation on cytogenetics and the histology consistent with the monophasic variant of a malignant spindle cell tumor are characteristic of synovial sarcoma.

rejected.label: Cardiac myxoma
rejected.why: Cardiac myxoma typically does not show the SS18 (SYT;18q11.2) translocation or malignant spindle cell histology.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
rejected.why: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma lacks the specific cytogenetic abnormality and immunohistochemical profile seen in this case.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Rhabdomyosarcoma is more common in children and typically has a different immunohistochemical and cytogenetic profile.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Leiomyosarcoma usually lacks the SS18 (SYT;18q11.2) translocation and the specific immunohistochemical markers seen in this case.
